utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Mr. Karadzic, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Before we do that just to finish up on the document we were dealing with yesterday that was placed under seal. First of all, I would like if we could give it a number; and secondly, I wanted to advise the Chamber that I communicated with the provider yesterday to ask them to clarify whether that could be used in public and I'll get back to the Chamber as soon as I have a response from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's very kind of you, Mr. Robinson. That's the step I wanted to recommend. Thank you. We'll give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1523 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Excellencies. Good morning to all in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to you as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your report -- or, rather, during the examination-in-chief, you dealt with the question of rewarding people in the police -- or, rather, awards being given to them. Do you agree that the president -- or, rather, the person who is conferring a decoration upon someone has to receive a proposal from someone? He cannot know himself who deserves that kind of decoration. So it's every ministry that makes certain proposals regarding their own people; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that the nomination process for that type of decoration or award took place through an internal nomination process in the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Serbian Republic and that not all of the people who were nominated by the ministry for such awards were persons personally known to the president of the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we briefly look at P2976. Let's see what that proposal looks like. Yes. That is one of the proposals. Do you agree? It's the public security station from Blazuj that is sending this to the ministry -- or, rather to the Ilidza station and then further on. Can we leaf through this? Actually, first of all you see this is a proposal to the -- rather, regarding the reserve police station of Blazuj itself that it should be decorated; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree and I would note that I cite this document in footnote 105 of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we just have a look at the next page and then the one after that, and we're not going to dwell on this document very long. A bit more, please. Further on so that we get to the individual names as they're listed. Gojko Keselj is being proposed here. Thank you. 1D3884, can we have that, please. Let's see yet another document, what the proposals sent to the ministry to the grassroots are. Unfortunately, there is no translation, but it's no problem for you; right? Do you agree that it is the chief of the centre of the security services of Sarajevo that is sending this to the ministry and it has to do with proposals for decorations and the signature is Zoran Cvijetic; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and I would point out that Zoran Cvijetic is nominating people on the basis of suggestions that he has in turn received from his subordinate public security stations in accordance with the functioning the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have the next page. Let us just see who all the nominees are. We don't have to look at each and every elaboration. Here it is, the list. And then after that there's an elaboration for each and every one of them, and that is sent to the ministry. Do you agree? And then the ministry sends it on to the president -- or, rather, to his office for decorations. They send a proposal that has to do with the entire republic; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and again, I find it important to note with respect to this page of the document that this entire exercise is being carried out within the Ministry of Internal Affairs pursuant, as we see in the document, to a dispatch issued by the ministry, the seat of the ministry, on the 23rd of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can this be admitted? For identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While there may be no problem with the witness to deal with this, there are a lot of problem with the Prosecution, as well as the Chamber, to follow the line of your examination. Why do you have so many uninterpreted documents, Mr. Karadzic, yet.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we don't have enough time, Excellency, but we do have quite a few translated ones as well. A great many more have been translated. However, this stemmed from the examination-in-chief, and that is why I wanted to have the witness's view as to these processes, how this is evolving from the very grassroots all the way to the ministry, and then the president receives a compilation, that kind of document, and this is one of the rare documents that hasn't been translated. We have lots that have been translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland. I noted you rose.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was to make the very point that you made. How can we deal with this properly and -- when we don't have a translation. It's an eight-page document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's concerning, but -- very well. We'll mark this for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1524, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like us to focus on the period of the war, how things developed during the war. Could we now have 1D3841. We do have a translation. It's coming. But you can read this, can you not? What does it say here? The deputy minister of the interior. That is what Mandic was far back as April. In paragraph 1 he says due to a major escalation of terrorism, violence, and looting in territories that are under the control of the MUP of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina it is necessary to organise patrols consisting of MUP employees of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the reserve MUP of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that vehicles should be seized from persons who don't have proper documents for these vehicles and that the crime prevention service should take urgent measures, et cetera, do you agree that already in April, on the 19th of April, the escalation of terrorism, violence and looting was recorded?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirm that that is what the document states.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted? Has the translation arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. I don't think we have a translation, according to the e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. We'll wait for the translation. Can we have a look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Bear that in mind that at certain point in time the Chamber may order you not to use the untranslated documents. We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI 1525.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I can just give you a little bit more explanation about why we have untranslated documents. The fact of the matter is that when the witness is being prepared for cross-examination, the case managers and Mr. Sladojevic accumulate a lot of documents and send them for translation and almost all of them are translated. However, Dr. Karadzic himself locates documents at the last minute based upon either the direct examination or other information that he's receiving in the course of his own preparation for these cross-examinations, and as a result those are the documents that are not translated. And that's why we continue to have untranslated documents even though we've improved our procedures quite a bit. But nevertheless there are documents that come to his attention or he locates at the last minute, and those are the ones that are not translated. So that's exactly the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There may come a time to deal with that issue more -- in a more comprehensive way, but let's proceed for the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This translation has arrived. If you wish, we can have it placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's proceed. Let's -- we take your word. Then we'll admit this. Give the number. Did we give the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI 1525, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have a look at D404. Do you agree that on the 15th of April of 1992, Stanisic issued an order for persons who commit looting, appropriation of other people's property and other illegal acts should be identified and subjected to the most rigorous measures, including arrest and detention. So looting had already started, but the MUP had also started taking rigorous measures. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that as of the middle of April 1992, as we see in this order, Minister Mico Stanisic of internal affairs was aware of the problem of looting and large-scale theft and that he issued this and other orders trying to address that issue. It was an issue that the ministry came back to in a recurring fashion throughout 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. 65 ter 18393. Could we have that, please. This is from the month of June. This is a security assessment for the entire republic; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and I cite this document in my report. It is in footnote 376.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You're very kind. Can we look at English page 7 -- or Serbian page 7, English page 9. Do you agree this has to do with Semberija and Majevica, and then it says -- can we have 10 in English? It says that in Bosanski Samac, Orasje and Brcko and also in Kalesija, Zivinice and Kladanj, there is a certain number of mercenaries from Sandzak and Croatia and Zengas, ZNGs, you know who they are, the National Guards Corps of Croatia, it's a police military formation; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirm that that is what the document states. I would just add that as I note in paragraph 264 of my own report, it is quite plausible that this report that we have in front of us was the end result of a 25 May 1992 RS government request for such a report by the ministry, and is therefore an indication that the ministry was functioning properly as part of the RS government.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We see here that new paramilitary formations have been established by the Croatian Army and they were transferred to the territory of BiH, and also, retaliatory measures were taken. Can we look at page 8 in Serbian and 11 in English. The third line in Serbian says that the Muslim TO assesses that Serbian TO does not have enough forces in this territory to hold the liberated territories under control. They are left to their own devices, and they are not under a single command, and therefore they are more oriented towards looting rather than warfare. Is that right? Is that what is registered here?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it states in the document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A bit further down it says in view of the disarming of Muslim extremists after the armed conflicts in Bijeljina, and there is a belief that in Bijeljina, in Janja, there are some infantry weapons that had been hidden; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is also correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Actually, we needed the next page in English, 12. I beg your pardon. There's a reference to the ZNGs here, the last page in English, HOS, the Red Berets, the Green Berets, and other paramilitary formations. Can we have 14 in English now and 9 in Serbian. The fourth paragraph from the top in Serbian says: "What is also evident are conflicts and the presence of various paramilitary formations, many of which are looting, seizing cars, and performing other crimes violating public peace and order, widely intimidating and terrorising citizens and the like. Sometimes they even attack public security stations?" Have you come across this kind of thing, namely that the police was helpless at the time and that it was even subjected to armed attacks?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of the fact that the police was subjected to armed attacks during this period from a variety of sides. In some cases as the police amply document in their own reports, they were extensively involved in combat activities with opposing forces from the Muslim and Croat side, and as is also indicated in this and other police reports, on several occasions the Bosnian Serb police in fact came under attack, even in their own police stations from Serb paramilitaries. That, for example, took place in -- I believe, Brcko was one of the places where that occurred in the summer of 1992. I would not, however, characterize the police as helpless as a general observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you come across information to the effect that Milan Panic, as prime minister of Yugoslavia, and I called upon the Muslims to return and also that I asked Panic to send me a capable special forces unit to arrest all these paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of certainly the arrival of a special unit from the Federal Secretariat for Internal Affairs, I believe, headed by Mr. Mico Davidovic that was tasked with assisting the Serbian Republic in Bosnia and Herzegovina, among other things, with arresting paramilitary formations. I'm also aware of the fact that at some point you in your capacity as the president of the RS called upon Muslims to return to certain areas, and I am aware of the fact that that call created dissatisfaction which was reported by the police among the Crisis Staffs in some municipalities to which those Muslims might return. I am not specifically aware of that taking -- that appeal of yours -- or both appeals of yours taking place in co-ordination with Milan Panic as prime minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1526, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have a look at 65 ter 18394. Do you agree that this is a document that was signed by the assistant minister for the prevention of crime? It's a very long title from the social -- times of socialism. It should actually be crime prevention assistant minister; right? So it's Dobro Planojevic. On the 5th of June, he is saying that special attention should be played to finding perpetrators of war crimes, documenting this, arresting such individuals, and so on, and then he's asking for documents, photographs, post-mortems. And he's also saying that as far as the treatment of civilians in war and prisoners of war is concerned, international law should be strictly observed. This was actually a week after I issued that order on paramilitaries and the observance of international law. Do you agree that this person, Planojevic, acted properly?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked a number of questions and I will agree with you a number of times. First of all, I agree with you that police officials, particularly the ones from the old period, were very fond of long titles for their offices. Second of all, I agree with you that this is an important document and that is why I cite it in paragraph 266 of my report, footnote 377, and I agree with you that your reading of the document is accurate and that Dobro Planojevic is indeed asking that the problems to which you refer be addressed and that this be done in accordance with international -- as he calls it, international law of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the first part he says that there are perpetrators who are police officers, which is unimaginable and cannot be accepted. So he's already noting that some of the police officers have become engaged in the perpetration of criminal offences.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. The police at this point were aware of the fact that in some cases police officers of the Ministry of Internal Affairs were engaged in the perpetration of a various number of criminal offences, including, in some cases, looting, the problem to which we referred a little bit earlier this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1527, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now look briefly at D477. It's already been admitted into evidence, but let us just remind ourselves what it contains. I don't think that's the document. This one refers to the Red Cross. So D477. You also knew, didn't you, that I issued a blanket permission granting the protection for representatives of the International Red Cross; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But that's not the document that I'm seeking. The one that I need is 65 ter 09243.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's Exhibit D447, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: That's what we have on the -- on the ... Yes, that's the one. We have the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is brief analysis of the work to date and basic guidelines for the future work dated 11th of July 1992. Do you agree? You are familiar with this document, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document that I have collected. It's a document that I cite in the report at paragraph 217, and I cite it extensively throughout my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have English page 15 and Serbian page 16. You see here that despite everything, Stanisic is saying that we have to do our job, because --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters cannot find the paragraph that Mr. Karadzic is reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, interpreters couldn't follow. Could you repeat, making reference to the passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Second paragraph from the top in the Serbian, and then the next sentence. So you have noted here that Stanisic is reporting that the government, the Assembly, and the Presidency's constantly asking for law and order to be reinstated and to prevent the looting and to provide safety and security for the citizens; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. That is what the document states, and as this and other documents show, it was a struggle throughout 1992 for law and order to be established on the territory of the Serbian Republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at Serbian page 20 and English 19, and I would like for you to focus on Planojevic's contribution to this. He is proposing his list of priorities, among which are, the fifth bullet from the top, which reads: "Undertake measures so that our members know exactly what they can expect in the event of their having committing a crime." And then it says, the priority in the process of documenting war crimes is to provide documentation such as an on-site investigation, photographs, expert reports, coroner's report, et cetera. So you have noted all this, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I note that in my report. And while we're on the subject, I would also note that in footnote 383 of my report, I deal with another RS MUP document on a very similar topic, namely establishing authority and the rule of law on a certain section of the territory of the RS, and I note that in that document, on the last page of the report there were handwritten remarks by you, and I quote, "Keep enforcing order and the rule of law."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now move to the next page in both languages. Simo Tusevljak says here that criminal reports - that's the end the first paragraph - criminal reports are filed against everyone. In Vlasenica, of the 73 criminal reports, 23 refer to Serbs. Then he says that "our primary task to document war crimes and to file criminal reports in such cases if they are committed by Serbs?" You have also noted that the position within the ministry itself was to document everything; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. That is what the document states. As I have, I believe, noted in the report, I find it significant here that Simo Tusevljak finds it necessary to emphasise that it is also necessary to document war crimes if they are committed by Serbs. This shows in conjunction with other documents that there were at least some people in the Ministry of Internal Affairs who did not understand that war crimes needed to be documented regardless of who the perpetrators or victims were.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now briefly look at P1096. This is just a week later, which shows that they were provided this information regularly on a weekly basis. So let's have P1096. Can we have page 2 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to the last sentence in the first paragraph where it says that the meeting was also attended by a representative of the Federal Secretariat for Internal Affairs of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. You will remember that that was this Davidovic person who, already in early July, was asked to make an assessment, and you will remember that by the end of July, he made arrests in Zvornik and Brcko, and he was doing also something in Bijeljina. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will have to correct your reading of this document. Number 1 refers -- this is not a kind of information report produced on a weekly basis by the ministry at the time. This is, as I noted in the direct examination, actually a report that summarises the findings of the previous document we saw, that is to say on the 17th of July, 1992, the RS Ministry of Internal Affairs issues a report summarising their meeting which was held in Belgrade on the 11th of July, 1992, and as the Court will have seen, and we dealt with it in direct examination, this particular document that we have in front of us now was sent to the president of the Presidency as well as to the president of the government or prime minister of the RS. The second point I would make is that the representative of the Federal Secretariat for Internal Affairs of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, who was in attendance at this meeting, was not Mico Davidovic. It was, in fact, Petar Mihajlovic, who was also working at the Federal Secretariat for Internal Affairs and who is mentioned in the report of Mico Davidovic, which I know the Defence produced for the Court's consideration last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have the next page? The last paragraph in the Serbian. It says that there was a lot of discussion about the participation of some paramilitary formations of which almost every single one has no single command, cannot be removed from the territory. Many of them are involved in looting. They are disturbing public law and order, et cetera. So would you agree that this was in preparation for the subsequent action taken by Davidovic?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that this document can be read in the context of the desire for the Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs in Bosnia and Herzegovina to combat paramilitary formations on the territory of the RS with the assistance of the Federal Secretariat for Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we just move to page 3 in English and 5 in Serbian. Do you agree that in the second paragraph in the Serbian it says that Dobro Planojevic's view were accepted to the effect that the priority in detecting war crimes should be well documented? So second paragraph in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that this document reiterates almost precisely the wording of the document by Tusevljak that we saw earlier. It is emphasised that war crimes need to be documented even if they are committed by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now have D448. Here we have the letter sent by the government to the Ministry of Justice requesting specific remarks and objections to certain decrees and laws.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 10 in the Serbian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in the third paragraph from the top it reads: "Within the scope of its activities --" page 13 in English. "Within the scope of its activities the ministry and its services should particularly identify how to carry out work in an organised manner towards collecting and processing the data and the documents concerning the crimes and the genocide committed against the civilian population."

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that that is what the document states. I'm glad that you corrected yourself at the last moment there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter 11811. All of this pertains to the activities in July. You would agree that there were quite a few activities being carried out in that period in this particular domain?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look now -- this is the 17th of July. Mico Stanisic is issuing to all security services centre chiefs, and he says that incidents of looting and war profiteering and other severe crimes that have an effect on the state of security and political situations of significance to the security situation. And then downwards it says that failure to respect this order shall be deemed as a severe dereliction of duty, which means that he is threatening the employees of the MUP with sanctions should they fail to comply. Have you come across this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm quite certain that I cite this document at some point in my report. I can't locate the precise footnote right now, but this entire topic that we are discussing is dealt with at length on pages 75 to 82 of my report under the heading, RS MUP and the Rule of Law in the RS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this is already in evidence. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have D1360. Can we please enlarge the paragraph in the middle, the second one from the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it has been underlined here that the questionnaire should be filled in in the security services centre by all people regardless of their ethnicity and they are specifically mentioning Muslims, Croats, Serbs and others? This is another order issued by Stanisic that relates to a questionnaire that has to be filled out, particularly when it refers to war crimes and victims of genocide.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is what the document states.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe you have seen this document; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I note that this is a document without an ERN, and I don't specifically recall seeing this particular document before, but I certainly see that it confirms many of the other documents issued by the RS MUP during this period, which I cite in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at the next page so that we can see the signature and the stamp. And attached to the document is a questionnaire form. This is the signature and the stamp. Next page, please, so we that can see the first page of the questionnaire. This is the questionnaire that needs to be filled out by persons regardless of their religion or ethnicity. Thank you. Can we now have 1D3855. Please focus your attention on this document which reads, Banja Luka CSB is sending this document to its subordinate stations. Actually, it's conveying Minister Stanisic's order relating to all members of the MUP who have committed criminal offences, save for political or crimes of thought before, or from the period when the war started, and this information should be provided before the 31st of July. Have you come across this document, which is dated towards the end of July 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I cite at least one version of this document in my report. It's a topic that I dealt with also in direct examination, and I confirm that your reading of the document is correct, and the authenticity and content of the document is further confirmed when we note that in the 1992 draft annual report of the RS MUP, we see that for the period from April to December 1992, the RS MUP in fact had put - and this is from paragraph 381 of my report - 6.167 police officers at the disposal of the VRS. Most of them reserve police officers. There were a number of police officers who were transferred, both voluntarily and involuntarily, from the police to the VRS in the course of the period from July 1992 until the end of the year, many of them for disciplinary reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please look at the next page. It speaks about the same topics but the language is slightly different. It's more elaborate, and it contains instructions to the subordinate stations. But basically the topic is the same; right? Zupljanin is requesting within the seven days of the receipt of the dispatch a report to be submitted about the measures that were undertaken.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct. The document is consistent with the fact that the communications and chain of command of the ministry are functioning properly from the centre to the regional level and then from there on down to the municipal level with reporting and orders moving both ways along that chain of command. And the document is further consistent with the phenomenon that persons who were suspected of having committed criminal acts or disciplinary infractions in the police were being transferred to serve in the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1528, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at D473 just briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe that you're familiar with this document as well. Do you remember this document? This is a summary which was compiled in August after the operation of the federal SUP together with Mr. Davidovic; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm looking at page 10 in English and 8 in Serbian, please. The last paragraph in the Serbian version, as well as in English, says that the situation in Bijeljina is relatively satisfactory, but in truth it is much worse than at first glance and here a reference is made to myself, to me saying the situation has worsened because some refugees have written upon the invitation by Prime Minister Panic. Would you agree with me that there should be an optimum time conducive to the return of refugees? In other words, that not every moment is suitable for the return of refugees.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another one of the documents that I cite several -- at several points in my report. It's a very important meeting of the ministry -- ministry's leadership in Trebinje in August 1992, and, in fact, I referred to it earlier this morning precisely because of the point you make that it shows there was dissatisfaction in Bijeljina about the return of Muslims to that area. I'm not an expert on refugee issues, so I do not know that I could agree that there is somehow an optimal time conducive to the return of refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thirteen in English, 11 in Serbian, please. Bullet point 3. It says that "The internal affairs bodies have been infiltrated by Vidovic whose criminal and otherwise antisocial behaviour defiles the reputation of the MUP ... ," do you agree? And then can we go to English 15, Serbian 12. I'm sure that you have noticed yourself that immediately thereafter an order was issued to disband regional special units; right? That's bullet point 7 where it says that the special units have been involved in some abuses. That's why they have to be disbanded. And it says that the criteria for detachment membership must be made stricter and the appropriate technical equipment must be secured. Do you remember that the centres had their special units and that already in August those special units were disbanded. The reason having been mentioned in bullet point 3 and that is that the bodies of internal affairs were infiltrated by criminals and that there were abuses on their part. Do you agree with all that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, you've asked -- or put to me a series of very complex issues. I will do my best to deal with them in the order that you address them. First of all, I agree with you that this is the information contained in the document. I agree, first of all, that the ministry shows awareness as it had already done at the 11 July meeting in Belgrade that there were criminal elements in the police, particularly in the reserve forces, and I would note in paragraph 213 of my report I quote a speech by Mico Stanisic even later in the year, in November 1992, at the 22nd Assembly session, where he essentially notes that the police had not only been aware of but, in fact, had, at least implicitly, permitted thieves and criminals, as he called them, to enter the ranks of the police in the early days of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina. As regards the paramilitary formations -- or, excuse me, the Special Police Units in the RS, this is a topic that I deal with in pages 65 to 71 of my report. I agree with you that efforts were made by July and August to shut down or disband a number of these Special Police Units, particularly at the municipal and regional levels. Many of them and their members were in turn integrated either into the Army of the RS or into the centralised RS MUP Special Police Brigade under Milenko Karisik. I would further note that the first months of the war were characterised by a proliferation of Special Police Units. It, at some points, appeared that anyone who had a few guns and a spare uniform was fond of getting a couple of friends together and calling themselves a Special Police Unit. This is something you, yourself, criticised in the Assembly when you noted the need for -- I think you called them little princes or local princes to be put under control and to no longer engage in the operation of such Special Police Units. Lastly, I would note that a number of the Special Police Unit members and, indeed, commanders who were very active from April to August 1992, and who were criticised by some authorities in the RS for improper conduct or callous conduct were, in fact, later promoted in the ministry and indeed received awards from the president of the republic. An example of that phenomenon that I gave in direct testimony is Ljuban Ecim of the CSB Banja Luka Special Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, do you agree with me that we Serbs are prone to smearing other people's names and being spiteful, which is all based on one's own personal interests? That's how we behave. You know us well. Wouldn't you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have those kind of negative stereotypes about the Serbs, but I am aware that you, yourself, in the Assembly on several occasions referred to your dissatisfaction with internal strife in the Serbs -- or among the Serbs and that in particular there was tension between, for example, Serbs from the Sarajevo Romanija region and Serbs from the Krajina region not least about where, for example, the capital of the Serbian Republic should be located.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree with me that the main division of Serbs in the Second World War was into Chetniks on the one hand and Partisans on the other or, rather, the proponents of the Soviet revolution on the one hand and the proponents of the monarchy, and that -- that was some sort of a curse that I wanted to eliminate by bringing peace and bringing former Partisans and former Chetniks together?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for that question. It allows me to come back to a point that we discussed yesterday. First of all, I agree with you that the main division of Serbs in the Second World War was between Chetniks or Royalists on the one hand, and Partisans on the other, and I agree that you and many of the people who were involved in the development of the ideology of the Serbian Democratic Party - you mentioned yesterday, Milorad Ekmecic, I would mention also Dobrica Cosic - viewed it and have written extensively about what they viewed as the tragedy of the internal division of the Serb Nation between Chetniks and Partisans. As I indicated yesterday, it is clear that, from the point of view of the Serbian Democratic Party, the goal was, as you say, to reach some sort of historical reconciliation between those two tendencies, if we will call them that, in the Serb Nation. However, I would point out that many Serbs, both in Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as in Serbia, Montenegro, and Croatia, have argued that the Serbian Democratic Party was much more closely affiliated with the Chetnik tradition than with the Partisan tradition, and that would, to some extent in my opinion as an historian, be borne out by the document that I cite in footnote 597 of my report on page 109, in which the RS MUP describes the SDS as the bearer of activities and means for the liberation of the Serbian nation, and the organs of internal affairs, so to say, first enter into the battle of the Serbian nation for liberation. As we discussed yesterday there was and continued to be in the 1990s, a tendency between the Yugoslav tendency in Serb national ideology and the more narrow Serbian nationalist tendency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that I am the result of that reconciliation? My father was a Royalist and my mother's family were Communists. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with your family's background, and I'm familiar with a number of families that share that background and that were in the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at D467. We will come back to this segment and when I say this, I mean guarding of detention centres and prisons. Let's now look at this document. I'm sure that you're familiar with it. The date is 10 August. The summer of 1992. Here Mr. Stanisic requests that detention and holding measures shall be applied exclusively within existing regulations in order to avoid and eliminate any abuses. Do you agree with me that it says here that the premises where were people are being held or detained must fulfill basic hygiene and health requirements and the security of collection centres shall be the direct responsibility of the Serbian Army. In other words, collection centres for prisoners of war and that also if they do not have enough men for these duties, it shall therefore be necessary to engage members of the reserve police for these tasks. Have you come across this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I had this document for review. Again, I note that it doesn't have an ERN number, and I do not immediately recognise it as a document that I have reviewed earlier. I would point out that this document is completely consistent with the concern of Mico Stanisic, as minister of internal affairs, with conditions in detention facilities and prisons at this point in time. As I noted earlier, as of the 11th of July meeting in the summer of 1992, there was an awareness in the RS MUP that conditions in many of those detention facilities were unhygienic and insufficient for the purposes of detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at D469. It has an ERN number, and I'm sure you have come across this document in which Mico Stanisic -- unless somebody signed on his behalf, which is very possible. In any case, Mico Stanisic mentions for the first time the existence of illegal prisons, and he asks the ministry to be informed immediately of the existence of those potential and official prisons and he wants to know who set them up. Do you agree with that? In the first passage it says: "I hereby repeat the order to all security service centres, public security stations and other organisations to act exclusively accordance with -- in accordance with the law." Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am familiar with this document, and I agree that that is what the document states.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at D109. Are you familiar with the document issued by the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which is entitled "We accept, we propose, we shall do." This is a declaration on the position of the Republika Srpska. Are you familiar with the document? Have you ever come across it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, let me just please say that the document we just looked at is a version of that which was actually a version forwarded by Stojan Zupljanin in the Banja Luka region, is cited in paragraph 311 of my report. He forwarded it on the 20th of August. As for the document that we have in front of us, that is not a document that I immediately recognise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can see, for example, that we say we shall not accept territorial claims by neighbouring countries, if any will accept to form, together with the other two national communities, a community of states of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the existing external borders and so on and so forth, and then it says we shall do, in the penultimate paragraph, where it says, "Any document on selling or giving up of property made under force will be declared null and void and without any legal validity." Do you remember that on the 19th of August, two days prior to this, I issued a document in the form of an order to make null and void all documents possibly signed by anybody in order to either sell or donate municipal property? Do you remember that document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with such a document. As regards the 19th of August, in paragraph 310 of my report I note that on that same day you ordered the VRS and the MUP to treat all prisoners in accordance with international norms and to co-operate with all international organisations, which was a reiteration of a presidential order of the 6th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at 1D3632.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a Serbian version? What we see now is two English versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that here somebody from the Bijeljina police made some claims about irregularities? The Ministry of the Interior then set up a commission, and the commission now submits a report. You can see the composition of that commission, and the report is about the allegations that were made. In the second paragraph it says it was concluded that the status of the fleet of vehicles, the depositor of goods and monetary assets, and the communications equipment in the Bijeljina SJB should be ascertained. Are you familiar with this document? Does the document speak about an attempt to clean the police ranks from anybody doing illegal things?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with this document. I agree that this document shows that a commission had been formed to investigate allegations of impropriety and allegedly criminal action by the employees of the ministry, and in particular, employees of the ministry in the Bijeljina area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at the last page and the signatures of the commission members. Do you agree that it says here in the second paragraph that following consultation with and approval by Undersecretary Cedo Kljajic, it is hereby established that Dragan Andan made a transgression, and there are also signatures by the three commission members; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm well aware of the ongoing saga of Dragan Andan and the slot machines on the territory of the RS in the summer of 1992. I confirm that this is a commission that was formed and I recognise the first signature being that of Goran Macar, who has also testified at this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1529, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before the break I would like to call up 65 ter 5295. We're moving on, and we're now in the month of September. 5295. This is it. Are you familiar with this document? Here, Minister Stanisic sends an order on the 6th of September, and he says, authorised workers of the Republic of Srpska MUP in performing tasks in internal affairs' domain by measures of confiscating objects, items, and so on have to do so exclusively in a way envisaged by the law. Valid confirmations on confiscated items must be issued. That should be enumerated, put in orderly evidence and treated as papers of value. And then in the statement of reasons, it says the reasons mentioned in this order have come out in by now in several cases of registered illegal relations towards confiscated objects and items, which causes great disapproval of damaged [indiscernible] and other citizens. Have you come across this document? And then in bullet point 4, he threatens the perpetrators by sanctions and punishment.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm very familiar with this document. I collected this document, and I also cited this document in paragraph 279 of my report. It's footnote 392, and I discuss its contents in that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1530, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we now look at D1356 just briefly. D1356. This is a part of my own diary, and the date is 14 September 1992. I would like to call up page 5 both in Serbian and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to where Stanisic says that there are over 1.000 criminal reports, and that was on the 14 September 1992. There were over 1.000 criminal reports. Do you remember that there was a constant sentiment of dissatisfaction with the lack of efficiency and the nonexistence of a legal system? Requests were made to establish courts that would be able to deal efficiently with such a large number of criminal reports.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of these sentiments of dissatisfaction with the rudimentary nature of the judiciary system, and I would note that there is a lot of virulent exchanges, "prepucavanja," between Mr. Trbojevic, and Mr. Stanisic, who very much disliked each other. Perhaps that's one of the elements of internal strife that you referred to earlier. With both the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of Internal Affairs throughout the period from April to the end of 1992 blaming each other for the problems that were being encountered with the establishment of the rule of law on the territory of the RS. I would just also note that in the very last section of my report, which is a summary of an interview with Mico Stanisic in the newspaper "Javnost" from the 30th of October, 1992, he discusses his own views of this issue as he saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now look at the following page in English. Do you agree that the rivalry between the services were a problem for the president of the republic, whoever that may have been, that -- that was quite a burden on state bodies, including the president, who had to be an arbiter between them?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly in any government when there are strong personalities and differences between ministers, that will create certain challenges for the prime minister, who is the president of the government in which those ministers sit, and for the Presidency that sits above the government. As to how much of a burden that was on the president of the government or on the Presidency, I would defer to your expertise there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look what Vice-President Koljevic is asking. He's asking about the confiscated cars, and can a special unit be authorised by the Assembly to go on the ground and make arrests? And then Mr. Djeric says, "War is chaos, but it is a fact that each minister must be held responsible." Have you had an opportunity to see this journal of mine?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I hadn't had an opportunity to see this particular journal or document, but I have had occasion to read the debates both at the government level and in the RS Assembly in the course of 1992, and I would note that everything that I see written on this page is amply reflected and amplified in the debates of the Assembly at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Is this the time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We will have a break for half an hour and resume at five past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you, Excellency. [Interpretation] Can we have now in e-court 65 ter 18407.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe that you are familiar with this document too. The Ministry of Judiciary and Administration is writing to the Ministry of the Interior, and in the first paragraph, the second sentence reads as follows -- I don't know if the translation is ready or not, but it says: "There are incidents in which Executive Committees are rendering decision on putting temporarily confiscated items to auctions which constitutes a violation of the law. The internal organs shall provide custody and guarding of the confiscated items in the manner determined by the competent court." And then it says that there are items whose owners are not known or are perpetrators of criminal offence, but even in such instances, the law must be abided by. Have you seen this document before? But since this was produced by the Ministry of the Judiciary, you probably didn't deal with this extensively. However, you can read our language, and you can see here on the first page that the Ministry of Justice is warning the Ministry of the Interior to make an effort and prevent unlawful treatment of confiscated items; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with this document. I have read it and analysed it previously. I confirm that your reading of the document is correct and note that it is to be read in the context of a widespread pattern in which persons, both private persons and employees of the Ministry of Internal Affairs had illegally disposed of property that have been confiscated by the police. In many cases, such items were transferred to the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and sold there for personal profit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we have the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, thanks to Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we look at the last page, please. Conclusion. It reads: "The securing of the facilities housing the items --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note that we do not have either the Serbian or the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have the last page in e-court, please. I don't know if this was properly translated, "by having control," which in Serbian is to dispose of, that is to say to use at their own will and as they see fit; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that's what the document states. It's in my view somewhat ironic that this document was produced by Momcilo Mandic, who at the time was the Minister of Justice since Momcilo Mandic himself subsequently became the subject of a number of investigations that alleged that he had been engaged in personally profiting from the sale of confiscated items, that is, items that have been confiscated on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina and which were being sold on the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that I established a commission chaired by Vice-President Koljevic to investigate the allegations against Maljevic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mandic, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- and that Koljevic, although he did not like Mandic too much, did decide that all of this was just slander?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with that commission and its findings. I would point out that was hardly the last commission or criminal investigation into those matters conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know that Mr. Mandic was exonerated of all charges for economic crimes and for war crimes by the Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was not too much favourably inclined towards him? I just wanted to point out that this is an illustration of how much we like to accuse each other and get involved in mud-slinging.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Mandic was exonerated of some charges. I believe that he was actually convicted on at least some charges. He did serve some time in prison, if I recall correctly. I would not agree with your characterization of the Court in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I would, however, agree with you that there are ample indications in various media that persons such as Mico Stanisic, Tomislav Kovac, Branko Djeric, and others have, for well over a decade now, engaged in finger-pointing exercises related to this and other allegations of criminal activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1531, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now have 65 ter 5286. This is now the month of October. Hopefully we have a translation. Yes, we do. Do you agree that here Minister Stanisic, and I believe you have seen this document, is ordering all security services centres and police stations where there are no direct war operations to withdraw the police from the battle-field in order for them to be able to carry out their regular police work. And then in paragraph 2, it says: "After having rationalised the reserve police work-force and after their transfer to the Army of Republika Srpska, the heads of centres and SJBs have an obligation to inform military commands that it was not their duty to send police force members to be transferred to the front line ..." Do you agree that the induction of law and order frequently depended on the fact of how many policemen were deployed on the defence front lines, that is to say how many of them were absent from their primary tasks?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I deal with this topic at length in my report and I cite at least one version of the document we have in front of us. Certainly from July 1992 all the way until the end of 1992, Mico Stanisic and other leading officials of the RS MUP are displaying dissatisfaction with the extensive involvement of the police in combat activities. In my direct examination I referred to the phenomenon dealt with at the 11 July meeting and again on the 17 July document. Both documents contain the quote that it's unacceptable that the police are in the trenches and the soldiers are conducting traffic check-points. So it is very much the case that Mico Stanisic is aware of the fact that this has a negative consequence on the functioning of the ministry and that he tries with mixed success to extricate the police from combat operations. When I say "mixed success," what I mean by that is that the draft 1990 -- 1992 annual report of the ministry demonstrates that until the very end of 1992 and, indeed, beyond that point the police continued to be heavily engaged in combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1532, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we briefly take a look at MFI D1371. Hopefully, it's been translated, but let us just remind ourselves of the extended meeting of the senior staff members of the 5th of November held in Bijeljina. I believe you've seen this document. So it's D1371. Do you recall this extended meeting of the senior staff members? Do you agree that a confusion can be created if you say "extended meeting" or if you say "extended senior staff meeting"? What we are talking here is an extended meeting; right? You speak our language. You can make the distinction?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you. The RS MUP during this period was not always very attentive to its use of language.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have page 3. Third paragraph reads: "Reminding of the conclusions from Trebinje, it has been underlined once again that members of the service can only be those persons who meet the requirements for working in the organs of the internal. We have to purge our ranks again from such individuals who are doing things that are not permitted intentionally." Have you seen any information asking check-ups of criminal records to be checked for people who have been nominated to work in the police?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a very interesting question, because, in fact, even when one reviews the personnel records of RS MUP in 1992, there do not appear to be a large number of documents that would be asking for criminal records to be checked or documentation of such criminal records to have been checked for people who were nominated to work in the police, which, as you have previously noted, should have been standard operating procedure in the police. I would note again that Mico Stanisic, as I noted earlier today, was well aware of the fact that particularly as regarded the reserve members of the police, a large number of unsuitable elements, including people he himself referred to as thieves and criminals, had been included in the reserve police forces of the RS MUP during the first months of its operation. I would also point out that the language in the paragraph that you just read makes it clear that this is a recurring phenomenon. They've discussed it in Belgrade. They've discussed it in Trebinje. Now they're discussing it in Bijeljina, and they still feel the need to keep reminding everybody in the ministry that this is an important issue that remains to be fully resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There are a number of folders containing between 500 and 600 pages, particularly in the Banja Luka CSB in which there are demands for various vetting procedures to be conducted for people who were nominated, and admittedly some of them did have criminal records, but some didn't. Did you have an opportunity to see those binders with these many pages?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have a recollection of seeing binders which correspond to what you are just describing, so I do not know whether those were available in the OTP collections at the time when I reviewed those collections. I would also be curious in knowing what the date of those vetting procedures were. As is indicated by the document in front of us, there were significant efforts made in the second half of 1992 which yielded some success, especially once 1993 started and the situation stabilised a bit. Efforts were made to vet those police who had been recruited. Already in the second half of 1992, large numbers of reserve police were simply transferred to the VRS as the most expedient method identified by the minister himself making the staff of the ministry manageable and transferring away from the Ministry of Internal Affairs those persons with inappropriate backgrounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it was more difficult to be in the army than in the police and that it constituted a certain degradation, not to say punishment, because working in the army was more difficult than working in the police?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we have a case where both the army and the police seem to be constantly disagreeing, particularly in 1992, as to who was bearing the brunt of the burden of combat activities, and there are indications of officers of the VRS accusing the police of harbouring people who are actively seeking police employment so as to avoid combat activity. Alternately, the police retorts that they are so involved in combat activity it is in fact the VRS that is relaxing while the MUP is bearing the brunt of the burden. In any case, it is clear that from the perspective of some people in the Ministry of Internal Affairs, transferring someone to the VRS was equated with some kind of punishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at page 6 which speak about reporting. Do you agree that there was a tendency amongst people not to report their own mistakes? So, please, look at the first three lines where the minister is instructed that in Zvornik, rigorous -- vigorous measures should be taken towards heads of the SJB, including their dismissal because of the mistakes and flaws in the process of reporting. Did you come across such mistakes in the reporting procedures?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are cases in which the minister expresses concern or dissatisfaction about insufficient reporting or inadequate reporting, and that is one of the reasons why the minister, in the course of the summer and autumn of 1992, sends out a considerable number of orders, instructions, and dispatches, all aimed at creating a better system of reporting. I deal with this on pages 71 and following of my own report. And it is also the case that Minister Stanisic sent a team of inspectors to visit the various regions controlled by the RS in an effort to make sure the police, both at the CSB or regional level, as well as the municipal or SJB level, was functioning according to the Law on Internal Affairs and the relevant regulations of the ministry. During the course of those inspections a number of irregularities were discovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is my assumption correct when I say that people are not very eager to report their own mistakes and transgressions and that they are prone to waiting for inspections to come?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I think that's the case not only in the Serbian Republic but in very many countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at P2761 just briefly. I'm interested in only two paragraphs that will illustrate my point. P2761. You've mentioned this report on work during the period from April to December 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cite this document extensively in my report and deal with it specifically in the section of my report from paragraphs 379 to 391.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm interested in page 14 in English and 19 in Serbian. Can they be displayed. Please pay attention to the fourth paragraph in the Serbian language. Let's see where that is in English. The most severe forms of crime -- there is awareness that the most severe forms of crime which appeared in this period for brutality, ruthlessness and other elements comprising it are others against humanitarian international law. The number of these crimes is surely much greater and the collection of documents is a difficult and long-term task. We have registered 101 crimes against humanity and international law?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please be asked to read slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you noticed that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the interpreters couldn't follow from a certain point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The paragraph begins with the words the most severe forms of crime. I interpreted it. I can read again but I believe that we all see it and we can all read it. I just wanted to ask the witness whether he noticed that there indeed had been awareness that those were the most severe forms of crime and that there had already been registered 101 crimes against humanity and international law.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took note of that, and I also cited that precise figure in paragraph 388 of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in footnote 4, it says that documentation was also collected by the National Security Service and the service for crime prevention; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and that was in accordance with the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at page 24 in Serbian. I believe that the page number's the same in English. It says here: Numerous actions were taken in order to document crimes, and so on and so forth. A total of 2.500 different expert analyses, dactyloscopies and similar measures were taken. Almost all crimes were carried out in CSB Banja Luka and some of them in Trebinje. Over 88.000 on-site investigations were carried out. Over 2.000 search warrants were issued. Almost 27.000 interviews were carried out. Do you agree with me that this is indeed an impressive result of activities that had taken place between April and December, especially in view of technical and personnel resources?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that this is a demonstration of a considerable amount of activity undertaken by the investigative organs of the RS MUP from April to the end of 1992. As to whether it is, in fact, an impressive result, certainly the employees of the ministry itself were proud of this result and included it in the annual report. I don't know how it compares to the number of similar investigative activities undertaken in the old joint MUP, so I'm not in a position to compare the level of activity. I do, however, know that the police on several occasions noted that despite the extensive activity undertaken by the police, a great number of problems remained in this and in other fields related to the work of the police and that's also dealt with in this report. And I would like to emphasise that this is an extraordinary document. It's very important to read it in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that to this very day judiciary proceedings are being carried out based on the reports that were filed during the war by the police of the Republika Srpska and the investigating judges of the Republika Srpska? All the documents have been preserved and court proceedings are being carried now.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware, based on information that I have from my colleagues in the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the RS, that in many cases court proceedings being carried out in 2011 do contain, in the court dossiers, information that was produced during the war by the police of the RS and by the investigative judges of the RS. I also know that my colleagues in Banja Luka at the ministry have on occasion pointed out to me that many of those dossiers languished in desk drawers of the police or the Ministry of Justice during the war and were only made the subject of thorough investigation at a much later date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at 65 ter 18346. And that would bring us to the end of the inspection of documents at the republican level. We would then move on to the municipal level. 65 ter 18346, I hoped it had a translation. Do you agree the document was issued while the minister of the interior was Ratko Adzic. In April 1993, he issued an order to all employees and members of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska who had unlawfully appropriated any goods to report that to their employer within ten days. Should it be established that somebody failed to do that and should stolen goods be found on their person, legal measures would be taken against them. The new minister inherited the obligation to purge the police ranks and to punish those who are in illegal possession of stolen goods. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The new minister, indeed, inherited the obligation to purge the police ranks and to punish those who were in possession of stolen goods. By the same logic, he also inherited a ministry in which such persons had not yet been purged. As of April 1993 this shows that the situation of which Mico Stanisic had spoken repeatedly in the entire period from April 1992 until the end of 1992, had still not been addressed to the point that it was no longer relevant. It's still an issue that the new minister has to remind his subordinates of in April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted or marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D1533, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now I'd like to draw your attention to a set of documents which refer to the functioning of the police in the security services centres. Do you agree with me that the Trial Chamber should know that that was the middle level? There was a ministry at the republican level. There were security services centres at regional levels, and there were public security stations at municipal levels subordinated to the middle level CSBs; right.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have testified to that effect. It's in my report, and it's also reflected in the organigrammes that are appended to the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at 65 ter 05297.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit P2765, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm sure that you have come across this document. It was issued in late July 1992. The chief of the security services centre in Sarajevo, Zoran Cvijetic mentions looting and large-scale theft and he says that -- the impression is that all that was the result of organised crime activities and that some police officers seemed to be involved.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this document and its contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we move on to the second page both in Serbian and in English. Yes, in English as well. Here the military police is described as searching civilian premises which they shouldn't do, and that some order has to be restored into that, that citizens report to public security stations that things like that are happening. Do you agree with all that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree that that's what the document states. It accurately reflects a situation in which there were a number of disagreements about jurisdiction and operations at the operational level between the VRS and the RS MUP, and that was the subject of discussions at the level of the -- of the leadership of both the army and the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now look at 65 ter 01595. This was also issued by the Romanija Bircani Security Services Centre in Sarajevo. Are you familiar with this document which says that an order was issued by the minister of the interior to disband the Special Police Units and to be resubordinated to the army and in the third paragraph it says that they should be removed from the territories where they are active and that refers to all the groups and the individuals who are not under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska. And those who have been disbanded have to be resubordinated to the army. And that all crimes should be documented, and that measures should be taken in keeping with the provisions of the Law on Criminal Procedure. Have you come across this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
