utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of this document, and it conforms to the process that we discussed earlier today, namely the effort undertaken after the 11th of July to disband Special Police Units that had been formed at the level of the SJBs and the CSBs in order that they be replaced by one centralised Special Police Unit. One salient point that I would also note for the Court's attention in the previous document that we examined is that document also notes that, because of the difficulties encountered in co-operation with the military police, the police had actually started to form joint check-points with the military police and that this had already ameliorated the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we move on to the following page in English, as well as in Serbian. The second paragraph in Serbian, as you can see here, a new order was issued that criminals should be removed from the Ministry of the Interior, especially those who were prosecuted ex officio, save for political and verbal offences. Do you remember that during the Communist reign the most common crimes against the state were the so-called verbal offences, whereas the new authorities do not punish such offences?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go to the following page in English, please. Penultimate paragraph and I'm reading from the Serbian version where it says that: "Proper measures will be taken against all responsible persons of the Ministry of the Interior who fail to act in accordance with this order." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that and I would note that the paragraph before that also notes that those who are being dismissed from the police are being transferred or put at the disposal of the Army of the RS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the Serbian version I would like to draw your attention to the first paragraph where it says that there were repeated complaints about lack of information. Is that correct? And it also says that the Ministry of the Interior should receive continuous and timely information along all the lines of work; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document contains one of many reminders I've seen in RS MUP documentation during this period emphasising that it is important to communicate in a timely manner, particularly with the seat of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1534, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at 65 ter 18273. Can we zoom in on the first article entitled "Critical Situation In Sanski Most." The first part of this page, yes. Thank you. Is this the 30th March 1992, on the eve of the first war conflict breaking out, and it says here that all those placing obstacles to investigations will be prevented from doing that. The MUP was still a joint organisation, and the question is raised why the joint MUP doesn't want to employ 150 people in the public security station in Banja Luka. Have you come across this information? Are you familiar with the hardships that existed at the time?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this document. I'm familiar that that was the point of view held by Stojan Zupljanin and many other Serbs in CSB Banja Luka and SJB Banja Luka as of the end of March 1992, and I refer in my report to their dissatisfaction with the operation of the joint MUP for many of the reasons that I already testified to yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Preventing investigation continues with the words that in a place called Dobretic, which was a Croatian village, the HDZ did not allow investigations to take place whereas the murderer was allowed to escape from the law enforcement agencies. Do you see that, the words are to prevent investigation.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that that is an incident that is discussed in this article. I would also point out that such incidents in which criminal investigations by the police in Bosnia before April 1992 were blocked allegedly by one of the three parties that formed the ruling coalition in Bosnia and Herzegovina or officials of those parties. Such incidents took place increasingly during the second half of 1991 and early 1992, and we can see Bosnian Muslims complaining of that with respect to Bosnian Serbs and Bosnian Croats, Bosnian Croats complaining of that with respect to Bosnian Serbs and Bosnian Muslims, and of course, Bosnian Serbs complaining of this problem with respect to both Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1535, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at 65 ter 05457. I believe that you have come across this document. This is a report -- or, rather, conclusions from the meeting of the Centre Council held on 6 May 1992. In other words, that was at the end of the first month of war. Did you ever see this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have reviewed this document, and it's cited on several occasions in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we go to the following page, please. Under 3 there is a reference to adopting stricter measures towards police officers and senior police officers. They have to start wearing berets. They have to set an example and serve as role models, whereas under 5 it says: "We have to identify in time those of us involved in criminal activities and we must take rigorous steps against them (immediately commence disciplinary proceedings)." I'm sure you noticed all that; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have the next page, please. That would be paragraph 15, so in English it's perhaps two pages further. Paragraph 15. Do you agree that it says that the documentation of the activities of war profiteers should be intensified and investigations should be started against them. "Operative processing" is the police term used here, I believe?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1536, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you can we have 65 ter 00798 now, please? Do you remember that you've seen this document as well? It's the 26th of May, again the Banja Luka centre. And in paragraph 1, it says that there are shortcomings in the daily reports. So very often information provided is not complete. Morning dispatches are not being sent on time. Incidents that are subsequently learned of are not being registered, and comprehensive daily reports are not being sent. Do you remember this report?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and I agree with your reading of the document. I would supplement your comments on the document by noting that Zupljanin, who was at the time the chief of CSB Banja Luka, is doing this pursuant to an order issued on the 16th of May, 1992, by Mico Stanisic, and this is one of a considerable number of documents that shows that both Minister Stanisic and chief of CSB Banja Luka Stojan Zupljanin were they intent on obtaining, in a timely and regular manner, all relevant information on the work of the police and on security events from the local and municipal level all the way up through the centres to the ministry itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We see here in the second part a description of these crimes. Can we have the next page now. Description of the crimes that have to be reported. It says under 23: Cases of the activation of explosive devices. And number 24: The number of cases of desecration of monuments, cemeteries and so on. Do you agree that this indicates that there was a war going on, explosive devices, and also monuments and cemeteries were being desecrated?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a analyst I, cannot based on this document alone, conclude that there was a war going on, although I, of course, know that one was going on. I would merely point out that as I noted yesterday, already by December 1991, that is several months before armed conflict actually erupted on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, well over 500 incidents of explosions had taken place, some of those involving attacks on residents but also some of them involving desecration of monuments, cemeteries, and the types of incidents that are also the focus of this information collection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that in 1991, a monument was blown up, a monument to our only Nobel Prize winner, Ivo Andric, in Visegrad? He won the literature Nobel Prize.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of the fact that that particular monument was blown up in 1991. I do, however, know that in 1991 a great many monuments, including many related to the Partisan movement and its exploits in World War II were being defaced or destroyed, a trend which increased after the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1537, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 00286. Do you remember that towards the end of May there was major fighting in the Sana River valley in the municipalities of Kljuc, Sanski Most, Prijedor, and Bosanski Novi? Muslim formations in the territory of the Sana River attacked these towns -- or, rather, the police and the military in those towns.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am generally aware that there were combat operations in that area towards the end of May. I'm not familiar with the details of those operations or any matter related to the question of who attacked whom. I only dealt with such operations to the extent that they were reflected in police documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that Stojan Zupljanin is asking here that the police not be engaged without orders, that they should not be involved in any kind of combat activity, not even in relation to the corps, unless this had been synchronised and set as such. Have you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen this document and Zupljanin's desires and orders are in harmony with the desire of Mico Stanisic as minister of internal affairs at this point to ensure that police forces would not be deployed without the permission of the ministry to engage in combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. The second paragraph says that any engagement or activity of the police is forbidden and so on; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1538, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a document that we've put in for a revision for the illegible name at the top in the handwriting. So that will end up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 05552. This is a document of the CSB Banja Luka, the 30th of July, 1992. It's being sent to all public security stations, to the commands of the 1st and 2nd Krajina Corps and also to the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and in the first paragraph it says that since the war had broken out, the situation is characterized by armed rebellions in the territory. I'm paraphrasing sort of. Then paramilitary formations are being formed, armed groups. There are acts of sabotage and terrorism against socially owned property and private property. Also the most serious forms of crime and looting, then failure to respect the law, civil disobedience, the unauthorised use of weapons, the dissemination of rumours and misinformation and so on. Have you come across this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am fully aware of this document, and I agree that it says what you just paraphrased it as saying. I would point out that as in many cases, I'm seeing the English translation of this document the first time because, as you know, I read the documents in Serbian, and therefore I think it should be pointed out to the Court that there's an error in the English translation in the addressees where it says on the third line of the addressees "MUP SRBH." That is not the Ministry of the Internal Affairs of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina but, rather, the Serbian Republic. Unfortunately, both entities used the abbreviation of SRBH or BiH, but certainly by the end of July 1992, Banja Luka was no longer reporting to the old ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You are quite right. However, you can never forget your first love; right? That's how the saying goes. Let's look at the rest of it. The last paragraph on page 1 says a number of active and reserve employees of the MUP taking advantage of the war are engaged in crime, illegally seizing property of citizens and so on. So Stojan Zupljanin is saying that among the ranks of the police there are persons who are actually committing crimes. Can we have the next page? What is described here is unlawful activities and also that it is impermissible to tolerate, as had been the case in some areas the escalation of crime. Then the second paragraph speaks about the operation called "Punkt," check-point. Yes, you have it in English here as well. Do you remember, together with the military police, the civilian police set up joint check-points in order to deal with these robbers and people who were taking away property that belonged to others?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this, and since you quoted a Serbian proverb, I would note that it would perhaps also be relevant to quote Stojan Zupljanin, who at one point said in an interview at about this time in the spring of 1992 that the Serbs had regarded the joint MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina as their mother but had felt as if they were being treated as if that ministry was their mother-in-law, "maceha."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have the next page in Serbian. In English it's fine. Do you remember that the army and the police believed that false patriots in the name of Serbs, Serb interest, and Serb freedoms committed crimes? That's paragraph 2. And in Serbian it's actually the next one. It says: These phenomena and activities are giving rise to bitterness and indignation. First of all, among the Serb people in whose name and in the name of whose symbols, appalling criminal acts, looting, arson, robbery and violence are being committed. Among other ethnic communities, this creates fear and unavoidably causes ethnic division and a lack of confidence in the institutions of the system. There is a realistic and objective danger that unless such occurrences are prevented, all control will be lost, which could have unimaginable consequences for the security of public order. So would you agree that there was an awareness that these were false patriots who were committing misdeeds in the name of Serbdom?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that that is precisely what the document states. At this point in the summer of 1992, by the end of July, we see a substantial shift in the attitude of leading officials of the Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs in Bosnia and Herzegovina towards such groups whereas in the period from April until June the presence and activities of such groups had been tolerated and, indeed, in some cases formed the subject of joint operations with the police. By the end of July, the police and its leadership was taking a very different stance that was aimed at bringing those groups under control, not least because they were, as is stated elsewhere in this document, beginning to carry out criminal activities in which case -- or in the cases of which in many instances Serbs, as well as others, were the victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, do you agree that at first people could not know who was prone to crime unless they actually did exhibit some criminal activity?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I cannot agree with that conclusion. As just one example of why I cannot agree I would again come back to Mr. Milankovic, who in September 1991 is featured in a document produced by Stojan Zupljanin in which he states - and since I had the opportunity to see it in e-court yesterday I now recall the precise number, was the subject of 54 criminal complaints that were pending against him. When he re-surfaces and co-operates in large measure with his group in the spring and summer of 1992, there is no question that the police knew precisely who that person was and were well aware of the fact that he and others in that group, as well as similar other groups, had criminal records. Unfortunately, the police in the Serbian Republic at the outset of the conflict took the attitude that those persons should be allowed, carte blanche, to undertake operations as long as they were doing so as "patriots." I believe that this precise conclusion of mine is also borne out by the extensive document which the Defence introduced last week during the testimony of Mico Davidovic and which I had the opportunity to review for the first time once it was introduced in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But do you remember from that particular document concerning the crimes of Veljko Milankovic that, basically, it was unlawful trades, smuggling of cars, and in countries that were under the Turkish or Austro-Hungarian empire for a long time, that is not considered to be a major crime to cheat the authorities, because our country was in that position for a long time in its history.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you'll have to excuse me for not being familiar with the precise age of Mr. Milankovic, but I don't believe he was alive at the time of during Ottoman or Austro-Hungarian rule and the crimes that he was alleged to have committed that formed the subject of the criminal complaints against him of which Stojan Zupljanin was aware in 1991 were committed against the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, among others. I would also note that I find this kind of relativisation of illegal smuggling, smuggling of automobiles quite curious as we just spent quite some portion of time emphasising that the police of the RS tried to take, with some delay, those precise criminal activities very seriously and to crack down on them even during the course of 1992. And as is revealed in the document produced by Mico Davidovic last week, it was the case that Milankovic and others in many cases entered the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and were engaged in ostensibly combat activities where they were literally being followed by trucks or even railway cars, onto which they were loading all of the assets that they were illegally confiscating, and then transferring across the border into the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia for personal gain. So much as it may be romantic to portray Mr. Milankovic as a "hajduk," I cannot agree with that characterization.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I agree, Dr. Nielsen, that Mr. Milankovic did not live in the times of Austro-Hungarian or Turkish occupation, but you will agree that customs and habits and attitudes towards state property live on longer than any empire. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we have the next page in English please, and we've already moved on to the next page in Serbian. So what we have here are orders. So that was the previous page in Serbian. "In order to overcome the situation that has arisen and ensure the efficient functioning the centre, I hereby order, order, number 1: "In the performance of their duties, public security stations as the organisational units of the centre may carry out only jobs and tasks falling within their competence in accordance with the law ..." And so on and so forth. I don't need to read all of it out, but do you see on this page these six orders that were issued by Mr. Zupljanin? And there are more orders of this kind on the next page up to 11. Were you aware of this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of this document, and I agree that it is saying what you read it as saying, and it is amply corroborated by many other documents with similar content produced by the RS MUP during this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to draw your attention to paragraph 4 where it says that what happened was that citizens were being arrested irrespective of their ethnic affiliation by unauthorised groups and individuals, and he is asking for that to be clarified immediately and that these persons should be released along with proper documentation.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have the next page, please, in English and in Serbian. Paragraph 7, what is asked for is to establish immediately whether paramilitary organisations exist and carry out various activities, and also competent military security organs should be informed about this. Then point 8, removing all check-points on main roads and other roads that have not been set up by the police and so on. Also 9, it has to do with criminal activities and public security stations and police stations themselves. And then 10, file criminal reports against employees of public security stations with the competent public prosecutors' offices. And 11: "Chiefs of public security stations may not carry out any personnel changes without the approval of this centre, "and so on. Can we have the next page, please. The end of July. That is to say, this was a rather lengthy order issued by Mr. Zupljanin, and it deals with an entire scope of security-related problems that they had to face. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1539, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We probably have time for one more 65 ter 5 -- oh, no. No. This is a translation. I beg your pardon. This is a -- 18492. That's the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You probably remember this as well. He is reporting about a joint action of disarming paramilitary formations, taking away cars, ammunition, technical goods, and so on. I have to ask you something, Dr. Nielsen. Did you establish yourself or did you take this from somebody else that it was only non-Serbs who were being disarmed in this area? In your report there is a reference to disarming of non-Serbs. However, documents show that Serbs were being disarmed as well, and in some municipalities it was only Serbs who were being disarmed, because probably Muslims and Croats didn't have any weapons.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my own analytical conclusions that are included in my report of which I am again, as I stated earlier, the sole author. Based on my review of RS MUP documentation and a small quantity of military documentation, from summer of 1992 it is clear to me that the police, in conjunction with the JNA until it left the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the TO, and later with the VRS, engaged in activities that were ostensibly aimed at disarming the civilian population regardless of ethnicity. However, as I discuss in my report, I see references to it, for example, in paragraph 200, and I know that there are other references to it in the report, the actual operations appeared when examined overall to have the impact of focusing on the collection of weapons from the Croat and Bosnian Muslim population, certainly in north-western Bosnia-Herzegovina, the area known as Bosanska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that as we had a front line that was about 1.500 kilometres, we had to carry out mobilisation to a maximum and that Serb weapons were legalised and were either in the police or the army? However, we were not forcing the Muslims to be mobilised, so the proportion may be the one that you referred to. However, if our Serbs were not in these formations, then their weapons were being taken away as well, and that is what these documents say, the ones that you referred to; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would point out that the document that we have in front of us is from the 18th of August, 1992, and that the previous document we examined was from the end of July, 1992. By the time we pass the middle of July, there are increasing indications that the Serbian police are involved in the confiscation of weaponry from Serbs in those cases where such Serbs are not serving in the police, the army or other official armed formations of the RS, whereas again it is important to distinguish between that period and the earlier period before the middle of July 1992 when Serbs in paramilitary formations, as well as Serb individuals who had arms and who in some cases used those arms to commit criminal acts were not the subject of attempts by the Serb authorities to confiscate their weapons. As regards your point about an extensive front line and in mobilisation, both of the police and of the army in which Serbs were the vast majority of such formations, and Muslims and Croats did not serve, I with agree with that characterization.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then just another saying of ours that you must be familiar with. Time was needed to see who was prone to crime, and in our parts they say, it doesn't snow that hills would be covered with snow, but to have every animal show its traces. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may respond in Serbian. [Interpretation] Well, that is certainly possible. However, in that case, I'd like to refer to yet another proverb, that sometimes it seems that the police behaves in a way that would correspond to the following proverb: This old woman is combing her hair regardless of the fact that the village is on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need a break to digest the proverbs. That will be exhibited as D1540, and we'll have a break. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I just note that this is another document that's put in for revision because the illegible name that is clearly legible in the document. That's the same as the other document I referred to. So that will be in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for your comment. Yes. We'll have a break for an hour and resume at five past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, 1.35. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.34 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. In the presence of Dr. Nielsen, I would like to kindly ask you to consider the possibility of allotting two sessions to me tomorrow. This is an important report that have 395 paragraphs, hundreds and hundreds of footnotes, and, indeed, I didn't get enough time. If I could be given another two sessions tomorrow, that would be greatly helpful in my dealing with all these important issues that I cannot do with other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please proceed as efficiently as you can, and we'll consider the request at the end of today's session. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just going to say the Trial Chamber may be benefitted from knowing that the next two witnesses are here ready to start, and on the current prediction for time estimates, then it would mean that one of the witnesses would have to stay, perhaps unnecessarily, over the weekend to complete their testimony on Monday if two sessions, two full sessions, were to be given, and perhaps even less than that. That's the situation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 65 ter 18299.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe that you made reference to this document, and I'm sure that you're going to recognise it as soon as you see it. I believe that this is a certificate, but can we have the first or the second page of this document in the Serbian. Maybe page 2. Yes. Are you familiar with this document? On the 11th of May, 1992, Radoslav Brdjanin, holding the position of the president of the Crisis Staff of the autonomous region of Krajina case under item 1 that the dead-line for the surrender of illegally procured weapons has been extended to the 14th of May, and then he goes on to say that this was done at the request of citizens from all ethnic groups who expressed a wish to avoid any tensions relating to the surrender of weapons and the JNA is also requested here to return draft-related documents to respective municipalities. So you'll see that a decision was made for the JNA to withdraw and as a consequence he's requesting the documents that they have in their possession to be returned to the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have been familiar with this document. It is a document that I've analysed. I may cite it in my report as well. And I would just like to take a quick moment to correct a mistake of mine from before the break. My esteemed colleague from the Defence very kindly notified me that in the heat of the moment I'd erroneously translated "Maceha" as mother-in-law and not stepmother. That must have been a Freudian slip on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1541, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, I'm going to try to show you as quickly as possible a series of documents that deal with the disarming, and in that context can we please have 65 ter 18302.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could please all unnecessary microphones be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch sent by Stojan Zupljanin to all public security stations. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It pertains to the confiscation of illegal weapons; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have the next page, please. We have a response to the previous dispatch by Simo Drljaca, who says that in Prijedor they have drawn up a plan but that it's not being implemented due to the outbreak of war and conflicts in the area but that nevertheless a lot has been done and that about 500 pieces of various weapons have been seized and that in spite of that they will try to continue this action successfully. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirm that that is what the document states with the caveat that it's not Simo Drljaca personally signing it. It has been signed for him by another person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're right. Thank you. Can we see the next page. The first page was a dispatch dated the 25th of May, but now we have the 14th of May, and is it seems about the same thing. After what they had received from Brdjanin, he is implementing this in relation to the stations, asking plans to be drawn up. And under item 6 it says that proper documentation should be submitted to CSB Banja Luka for verification and that the results of the planned activities should be submitted on a daily basis by 10.00. Can we have the next page. Number 2, carry out this in accordance with the law. Anyone in violation should be subjected to criminal report? And now we have another document dated 18th of May. This is the reply from Simo Drljaca, and it says that there are paramilitary formations in Prijedor municipality as follows: Ljubija, and Donje Ljubija, a regiment armed mainly with small arms and sniper; Rizvanovici, Hambarine and Biscani, a company; and Carakovo, a company. All of this was happening on the 18th of May, and these formations attacked Prijedor on the 28th or the 29th of May. Did you have any information that at the time -- at that time there were paramilitary formations in the area of Prijedor that could not have been disarmed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just note that Mr. Karadzic is giving evidence again. And I don't object to these two documents, this one and the last one, but note they weren't on the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, not the 65 ter list, the list of documents to be used with cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may respond. The reason for that is that from one of the answers given by Dr. Nielsen, it could be inferred that non-Serbs were the ones who were predominantly disarmed, and I'm presenting to him a number of documents that he may not be familiar with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So, are you familiar with this document, or did you know at all these two -- these four local communes in Prijedor, armed formations existed on the 18th of May that Drljaca was not able to disarm?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with both of the documents we have just viewed, and I would point out the previous document from CSB Banja Luka is cited in footnote -- I believe it's 224 of my report in paragraph 202 where I deal with this period and this topic. I am aware of the fact that Simo Drljaca and other police in the operational area of CSB Banja Luka during May 1992 assert that had they were trying to deal with paramilitary formations such as the ones indicated in this dispatch. I am not in possession of information as to who are in these paramilitary formations. I note that the document does not say anything about the ethnicity of the members of these paramilitary formations, and I do not know what, if any, activities these particular paramilitary formations undertook in or around this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Court deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI D1542.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now take a look at 65 ter 18304. Are you familiar with the name of Vladimir Tutus who was the chief of the Banja Luka public security station?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Yes, I am familiar with Vladimir Tutus, and with his recurring disagreements with his boss Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But Stojan Zupljanin did not replace him or dismiss him.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is dated the 30th of September, 1992. Can we have the next page, because this is a covering letter and the document itself is on the next page. Do you agree that they are sending information here about having confiscated a total of 202 pieces of weapons, and on the next page we can see the breakdown of the weapons amongst which were also mobile radio sets. Can we have the next page, please. We see that they have also seized 25 radio sets and so on and so on. Paragraph 4, it says that misdemeanour reports were filed for possession, whereas criminal reports were filed for either preparation or commission of hostile armed attacks. And the last line in the Serbian. We need the next page in English. It says 43 criminal reports for the crime of illegal possession of weapons or explosive devices. So you will agree that misdemeanour report is slightly lighter, whereas criminal reports are always filed for more serious felonies such as possession -- illegal possession of arms or explosives and preparation of armed operation?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I agree that there is a difference in gravity between criminal complaints for -- or on misdemeanour charges and criminal complaints on criminal charges or felonies. Here I would note that at least, as I scan this document, it seems to me that in some cases the illegal possession of weapons was the subject of misdemeanour charges, whereas in other cases possession of weapons was the subject of criminal charges, but I agree with you that the gist of the document is that the police is reporting on the amount of weaponry that it has seized from various individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have page 6 in Serbian, and I believe it's the same page in English, and there we're going to find the list of names and their ethnicities. Let's look at nationalities. Serbian, Muslim, Serb, Serb, Muslim, Serb, Serb, Serb, Croat, Serb, Serb, Croat, Croat, others, probably Ukrainian or somebody else, Serb, Croat, Croat, Albanian, Serb, Muslim, then three Croats. Next page, please. Muslim, Muslim, Serb, Muslim, three Croats, Muslim, Croat, Serb, and finally five Muslims. And we need the next page in English. And there's a remark at the bottom. It says that they were arrested and placed in custody on the ground, that there was suspicion that they were preparing armed rebellion by procuring and hiding it -- obtaining -- TO. Public prosecutor redefined this criminal offence into illegal possession of arms, which is a lighter offence than armed rebellion. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next page, please. In both languages, and I think that's the very end of the document. And under number 31 we can see that criminal reports were filed against four Muslims, and we have a Muslim, a Croat, a Serb, Albanian, and so on. Do you see that this was signed by Vladimir Tutus and that there are quite a few Serbs here who had been disarmed?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that's what the document shows. May I please see the first page of the document again? The next page. The first page of the list, actually, of persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Six in Serbian. I believe that's the case in English as well.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as an analyst, one comment that I would just like to add to this document, and I agree that it shows what you say that it shows, is that if we look at the column in which it is stated whether those persons who had possession of illegal weapons were also detained, there we see an interesting pattern that for most of the Serbs in this document they were not detained, whereas most of the persons of other nationality who were also charged with the same crime, they were, in fact, detained for some period. So I think that is a significant point to draw out in this document as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The next page now, please, so that you can see that a Serb was detained too. Do you agree that they did not expect the Serbs to start an armed rebellion, but they did expect the Muslims and the Croats to do that, and that was a sufficient reason for detention; right? You see this here? Klasnja, Nenad, a Serb from Laktasi, detained. Number 6.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly agree with you that the authorities of the Serbian Republic did not expect Serbs to start or engage in any armed resistance against that republic, and in the isolated cases in which Serbs did engage in any such resistance, the authorities, based on the documentation I have reviewed, were often quite confused as to what to do about such resistance, whereas in the case of Croats and Muslims who were resisted the authority of the Serbian Republic, there as you, yourself, noted, that was sufficient reason for detention in most cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we look at the last page, another Serb detained as well, Dubravko Kuzmanovic. The last page, 34. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1543, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now have 65 ter 21816. Please cast a glance at this. All of these are Serbs; right? Copic, Dusan; Asic [phoen], Dragoljub; Gordana Petrakovic, see, even she has a pistol, but it was taken because a murder was committed; Cedo Stevandic, it was confiscated because he was carrying it without a permit. And then further down you see hunting guns and a carbine, the last one, Majstorovic. He had a carbine. All 17 of them were Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will take your word for it that all of the people on this list are Serbs. I would note however that in many cases it appears that these people had their weapons confiscated as early as 1986 in the case of the fourth person on the list, for example, and a lot of the other confiscations of weapons here appear to have taken place -- well, there's even one from 1978. There are several people here who have weapons confiscated from them long before the war. So this appears to, by and large, be dealing with weapons confiscations that have nothing to do with what is going on in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But he is answering, replying to this telegram, and you are right, they -- but they're all Serbs; right? They didn't return them to say the least. If they confiscated them in 1991, they did not return them; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they certainly didn't return them to person number 14 since she apparently committed suicide, but as for the rest of the people on this document, it's clear it appears that they still have these weapons in their possession. What I would as an analyst want to know here would be to go to the dispatch that the chief of the police in Drvar has, at some point, received. In fact, on the 3rd of November 1992 received from CSB Banja Luka. He is responding to some sort of request and I would be interested to go back to that CSB Banja Luka dispatch and find out what was the exact question or type of information that the SJB in Drvar was asked to provide.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I hope that we are going to come across that dispatch.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1544, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now have 65 ter 183110 [as interpreted]. Simo Drljaca is referring to the dispatch of the 3rd of November, and he says: We hereby inform you that for the time being this public security station has not confiscated any weapons on any grounds. You'll be duly informed if and when that happens. So the question was probably: What have you kept? What seized weapons have you kept? Does that sound right to you?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be my inference as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1545, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now have 65 ter 18312. This is from Bosansko Grahovo. It's also a reply to the dispatch dated the 9th of November, and it says that "we currently have the following weapons that have been seized." This seems to be a telegram that is asking for results, the results of the seizure or confiscation of weapons and which ones have been retained. So there is one person here who committed suicide - I'm not going to mention his name - so an automatic weapon was taken when another person committed suicide, and then there is this pistol when there was an attempted murder, and then, again, can you not see that all of them are Serbs, Ilija Branko, son of Obrad, Simo, Borisa, Stana. Nine, Stana, she has a soldier's rifle. There is this old granny who has a rifle. Will not give way. Jovanka. She must be a Serb too. And Grizelj, maybe they can be Croats. Have you come across this document anywhere? Not a single Muslim.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I note that this document has an ERN number beginning with a B which indicates to me that it's from the OTP's Banja Luka collection, so I can tell you right away that I have reviewed this document because I reviewed all 143.000 pages in that collection. As regards the specific document's content, I agree that it shows weapons that are being confiscated on the grounds of illegal possession in a number of cases because there is a suspicion that those weapons have been used to commit crimes, in some cases suicides, in some cases might be used to commit crimes in the future and therefore being confiscated. And I agree with you that there are no names on this list of 14 or so people who are Muslims. I would point out that that might, given the date of this document, have something to do with the fact that there were not that many Muslims left in that municipality at that time but that's conjecture on my part as I'm not familiar with the demographics at that instance in time of that municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1546, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 65 ter 00299. They're reporting from Kotor Varos in reference to the same requests on the 3rd and the 18th of November. These people are replying on the 1st of December and saying what has been seized and if you look at the names there's Christian and Muslim names, there's a mix; do you agree? There are Serbs and Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next page, please. There are quite a few persons unknown. This must have happened during combat. NN means unknown; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have the last page. We see the stamp and the signature, and we see that 131 items are there -- or, rather, 131 weapons that were seized from Serbs, Croats, and Muslims. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you. I would note that there are a relatively large number of hunting rifles that were confiscated here, and one thing that is quite interesting in the document is that it appears that in this case or in a number of cases of these 131 weapons, they were confiscated even though it says in the right-hand column that the owners had weapons permits for those weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I agree, but does it not seem to you that the owners themselves surrendered these weapons? Look at this one, automatic rifle, Spagin, unknown owner. Probably without a permit, and as for the rest, it's probably the owners themselves that came and handed over their weapons when the police station called for that. No one probably wanted to hand over an automatic rifle. They just cast them away as this Spagin did. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's conjecture, but I can see why you would engage in such conjecture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1547, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have just two more documents and then we're done with this topic. 65 ter 18315. It's the Bihac station. It's probably the Serb municipality of Bihac and the Serb station of Bihac and all of these people are Serbs and automatic rifles were taken from them. Jecmenica, Nikola; Petrovic, Ratko; Arsic, Bane; ah, there is one Muslim: Smajo Kavaz from Sarajevo. Then Zorica Medakovic and as a matter of fact, even this Smajo was in a group that identified themselves as members of the Serb guard, but they were caught committing a robbery. And then Mico Gogic's hunting gun was taken away. He was from Bihac. And he was disturbing public law and order. This was probably celebratory gunfire and that is why they took away his rifle, because of this offence. Would you agree with the way I have portrayed this document? Also, it is only Smajo Kavaz who is a Muslim; right? All the rest are Serbs.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that you have accurately summarised the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1548, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Another one -- actually, two more. 65 ter 18316. This is Krupa Na Uni, the former Bosanska Krupa, so it's the right bank of the Una. It is their public security station, and these are Serbs, Majkic. Their weapons were seized. Do you agree that Veljko, Sojka, and Uros are Serb names?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, could we please have the next page for the benefit of the other participants. Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1549, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 18308, just that one, and then we should be done. Again, there's a reference to the dispatch of the 3rd and 18th of November, and this is a reply to this dispatch. First, it is Smajkanovic Emir, who is a Muslim. Secondly, Momir Vujancevic, a Serb, an automatic rifle was taken away from him. Enes Meldic, a Muslim. Four, Pante Devic, a Serb. Goran Milisavic, a Serb and Gostimir Maric, a Serb. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Serbs in the lead, 4 to 2, as far as this disarming is concerned; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular document that is the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1550, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now briefly have a look at D474. I believe that you've already seen this document where Stojan Zupljanin is forwarding an order for Minister Stanisic to public security stations for the umpteenth time probably. This is an order stating that civilians, refugees should only be treated on the basis of the law and international law and international convention, et cetera. The last sentence says: "... it is necessary to proceed immediately with gathering information and documentation in order to submit a criminal report to the competent Office of the Prosecutor." Have you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may be permitted to refresh your memory. We dealt with this document earlier today, and as I noted, it's dealt with in paragraph 311 of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Oh, you're probably right. We dealt with the minister's document, but this is Zupljanin now forwarding that same document. Well, yes, you're right. Thank you. 65 ter 18419. Can we have a look at that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did we deal with that document today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document that was just on the screen a moment ago was a document that I comment -- commented on this morning. It's possible that it was with a different 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you seen this document where Zupljanin is addressing all the chiefs of all the public security stations, and he is asking them to do the following -- look at the third paragraph. There is some information indicating isolated individuals might be attacked or threatened in some way after their return to their home areas, so those who had been in detention. He's saying once they are released and returned there, that their safety should be ensured. Do you remember this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have a very clear recollection of this document, which is footnoted in footnote 459 in my report, again paragraph 311.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1551, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 65 ter 18419. Can we have that, please. I beg your pardon. This is a translation of the one we've had just now. 65 ter 55980.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 5598. 05598. Do you agree that Zupljanin is asking here for a selection to be carried out amongst the detainees. If proceedings are not going to be initiated against persons for whom there is no evidence, they should be released, and civilian authorities should take care of them, and you are probably familiar with this document as well.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, it is the next footnote in my report, footnote 460, again paragraph 311.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1552, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now have 65 ter 5506. Are you familiar with this document dated the 23rd of June, and what is mentioned here is that during a regular check during a police patrol a certain number of policemen, as they were checking traffic and passengers and their property, and there's a reference to all their names, the driver and the other person who was in the car, and on the basis of the behaviour of the passengers and when they examined the luggage that was there the policemen checked it in detail. Do you remember this document? A large number of foreign currency. These persons admitted to the policemen that they were reselling foreign currency, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We're still dealing with the CSB Banja Luka. We haven't moved on to the public security stations yet.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no objection to the document, but I think it should go for revised translation, because the date appears to be missing, the 23rd of June, 1992, under the "brod," number, in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, we'll admit this with that caveat.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1553, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now have 65 ter 17755. Do you agree that in the first paragraph here it says that the army is again asking for the active and reserve police to be actively involved in protecting the corridor and at other front lines too? Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this document, and I agree that that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The second paragraph it says that the number of reserve policemen has been reduced to the lowest possible level so that those who are released could be sent to the army. Do you agree? And then further on in the next paragraph it says that the area of the centre is threatened by a large number of sabotage groups of varying sizes, attacks from dispersed enemy formations, increasingly evident forms of war profiteering, criminal activities of individuals with the most serious consequences, daily threat to citizens' personal security and property, and other types of threat and disturbance. The general public knows about the group atrocities committed by enemy forces again the civilian populations in Prijedor, Sanski Most, Skender Vakuf, Jajce, Kotor Varos, and other locations. Do you know, Dr. Nielsen, that at the end of September there were still groups, hostile enemy groups, in depth of Serb-controlled territory and that they were still killing people?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with the fact that the police during this period is still reporting on the existence of such operations, and this is one of a number of documents that deals with that topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1554, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now see 65 ter 18405.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could Dr. Karadzic please slow down when reading from a document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you are reminded yet again by the interpreters to slow down when you're reading out documents.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document which was issued on the 19th of September? This is a minister's order on safekeeping deposits, i.e., safekeeping confiscated goods and issuing receipts and also on handling confiscated goods in a legally prescribed way. The title is: Reference order by the minister of the interior. And the contents are what I've just told you, and that is the courts need to be notified about confiscations of goods and certificates have to be issued and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1555, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now see 65 ter 18472. I believe that you are also familiar with this document, which was issued on the 19th of October. This is a -- an official note dealing with the activities of the Radical Party clashes, misunderstandings between the military police and the civilian police, and it says here that the main initiators Tomo Delic, a former SDS activist and so on and so forth. And further down, it says: The current conflict between the army and the civilian police is becoming worse every day. Lieutenants -- Lieutenant-Colonels Oljaca and Kamber have been involved in shady dealings. Now you can see how Serbs are involved in mutual slandering each other; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that I would agree that they're involved in mutual slander, but it's clear that at this point in time and, indeed, as witnessed in other documents for a significant period before that, there are a lot of conflicts among some very strong and ambitious personalities. In many cases, this relates to the issue of war profiteering which it is dealt with here, where it is clear that a number of individuals - I would say a considerable number of individuals - very diligently used the situation brought upon by armed conflict to enrich themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we go no the next page in Serbian and in English. We can already see it in the penultimate paragraph towards the end, where it says that Muslims are being helped to cross over to the Croatian territory in exchange for money. And then it says around 20.000 Muslims have moved out of this region and the remaining 10.000 or so wish to do the same, because of the feeling of uncertainty and lack of safety, and this is due to the wilful behaviour of individuals and groups who abuse citizens of Muslim background. I'm reading in Serbian. Do you see all that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that passage and I deal with a similar topic in paragraph 352 of my report where I discuss the awareness of the RS National Security Service of the departure -- of what they called massive departures, in their own words, of Muslims and Croats from Prijedor municipality. This is a case here where we, again, see an awareness of the departure of large numbers of Muslims from territory under the control of the Serbian Republic, and it contributes, together with other documents that I've been able to review, to an overall situation in which the police, as I stated previously in my testimony, either was unwilling or unable to provide adequate security to citizens of the RS who were not of Serbian nationality, and that is reflected here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it says in the penultimate paragraph that they are being transferred to Croatia in exchange for money, and do you agree that police officials record that? They do not attempt to sweep that under the carpet.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the case of this document that appears to be the case. There are other documents about the departure of Muslims and Croats from the territory of the RS in which it seems to be the case that certain persons were involved at the municipal level in confiscating or charging those persons before they were permitted to leave the territory of those municipalities, charging in the sense of charging them money.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, we do agree that the operatives have a negative attitude towards that, that they record the events and that they report on them; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and again I would refer the Court to paragraphs 352, 353, and 354 of my report where I deal with similar reports by the National Security Service published in 1992 and 1993 -- or not published but produced. These were very confidential documents at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1556, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now see 65 ter 05676. Are you familiar with this report covering the period from April to the end of 1992 for the security services centre in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am very familiar with this document. I believe that I cite it repeatedly in my report, and I would note that the contents of this document, when read in conjunction with the draft 1992 annual report of RS MUP, show that much of the information pertaining to the area of CSB Banja Luka, that ends up in the draft annual report stems from this report here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go to page 3. It actually may be page 2 in English. It says here the public security sector, and I'm looking at line 5 or 6, where it says that extremist activities by groups and individuals is aimed at undermining social order, sabotage and terrorist activities are targeted -- are targeting facilities and civilians. There are incidents undermining public law and order. There are attacks against police officials. There is a large-scale social disobedience. Rumours are being spread. The greatest forms of crime are rising in numbers. There are other forms of socially destructive behaviour, and so on and so forth. This is a terrible image. Does this reflect what you noted as conditions prevailing amongst our population at that time?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this document is an accurate reflection of the cumulative state of the security situation on the territory of CSB Banja Luka during this period. It accurately collates and summarises information contained in other documents produced in the period from April to December 1992 by CSB Banja Luka. As regards the exact choice of words and expressions by the authors of this document, I would note that they were very deliberate in their choice of referring to certain activities as being of a terrorist or sabotage nature and others of -- of being -- of -- of a more lawful nature. And I have to admit that I was halfway expecting you to tell me whether you also thought that the illegal arming that's referred to here was in the spirit of the Partisan tradition or whether it is a case that the police is duplicitous in its -- or inconsistent in its use of the term "illegal."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, you saw that the public prosecutor changes the qualification of the crimes reported to him. We saw it in one of the documents where it says preparations for rebellion is what he called unlawful possession of weapons. Wouldn't you agree with me that the police do not have the last say in all that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that when the police has an investigative finding that indicates that illegal activities have been occurring, then that information ultimately is transferred to the public prosecutor who can decide whether to follow up on those charges, change the nature of those charges, or drop the charges entirely. My comment here was perhaps insufficiently clear. Let me state it very explicitly: What I think I'm referring to here is that there is a tendency to refer to the arming of the Croat and Muslim population as being illegal, whereas the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the RS in referring to its own activities or activities carried out in conjunction with the SDS prior to April 1992 in arming Serbs also refers to those activities as being illegal, but they are rendered somehow legal in the eyes of the RS MUP once that entity, the Republika Srpska, is established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at the following page in Serbian, and perhaps it is the next page in English as well. Let's see what it says with regard to the following page in Serbian. There has been an escalation of sabotage and terrorist activity and illegal arming of Muslim and Croatian extremists. You would agree with me, Dr. Nielsen, that the Serb police did not expect the Serbs who were in possession of illegally obtained weapons they would organise themselves and turn against their own authorities, whereas they expected that from Muslim and Croat Serbs and their expectations proved to be justified. Would you say that therein lie the difference?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would tend to agree with you that such were the assumptions in the minds of the police officers of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina at that time, and I would note that it was precisely such assumptions that proved very consequential for the population, and particularly the non-Serb population, of the RS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's look at page 6 in Serbian where a reference is made to illegally armed Serbs, what is expected from them, and what they do. Look at the paragraph starting with the following words: "Under the conditions of radical aggravation and constant complication of the security situation, criminal activities by armed groups and individuals of Serb ethnic -- ethnicity has escalated, and activities of criminal groups and individuals leave an impression of anarchy among the general public which undermines the reputation and leads to the creation of mistrust towards the legal institutions of the system. There are break-ins and unlawful appropriation of different goods under the threat of arms ...," and so on and so forth. So they are aware that Muslim and Croat armed groups pose one kind of threat, and that Serb armed groups and individuals pose a different kind of threat; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not comment on that statement other than to say that I think this document and the language it uses speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The following paragraph also speaks about Serbs, groups, and individuals whose goal is to win power in an illegal way. And the last sentence says -- can we see the next page in English. Undertaking measures and activities keeps under control and then the following paragraph in -- on the same page speaks about the hooliganism, vandalism and other forms of destructive behaviour, which are under the strong influence by war and political events and very often develop into a phenomenon bordering on escalation out of control. So what is said here is that the behaviour of Serb or -- Serbian criminals and renegades is also closely monitored and kept under control.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the entire period from April 1992 to December or the end of 1992, it is absolutely clear in the documents produced by RS MUP that all kinds of criminality, everything from personal physical assault to burglaries to grand theft auto to, essentially, rapes, all kinds of criminality, increased dramatically across the territory of the Serbian Republic, and the police was very, very concerned about how to get that situation under control and to re-establish some kind of law and order on the territory of the Serbian Republic. That is reflected in this document, and it's reflected in other documents. What is categorically different in the documentation that I've been able to review is the types of measures that were taken by the police with respect to what you, in your question, call destructive behaviour when such behaviour was engaged in by persons of Serb ethnicity as opposed to the types of measures, many of them pre-emptive or proactive, to say the very least, that were taken by the same police force with respect to persons of Muslim and Croat ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's look at page 10 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would appreciate the correct page reference in English as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that we're on the right page in English. I believe that we're on the right page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us look how many criminal reports were submitted to the public prosecutor's office. A total of 6.802 criminal reports against 3.887 persons were filed with the competent prosecutors' offices. Of the total number of those reported, 586 person or 15 per cent --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot interpret figures at such speed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the interpreters couldn't follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Seven thousand and six hundred and eighty crimes were perpetrated by unknown perpetrators of which 3.512 were detected subsequently. Out of the total number of crimes, 4.166 were not elucidated, which is 50.7 per cent were detected. Do you agree that a large number of criminal reports, 6.802, during the nine-month period is quite a large number? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could Dr. Karadzic provide references when reading [overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is certainly a considerably number of criminal reports, and as the police indicates, I believe, elsewhere in this document and in documents we saw earlier today, they were aware of the fact that even with such large numbers this was most likely a significant underreporting of the total amount of crime that was being committed during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are on page 10. Please look at the fact that 46 crimes were committed against humanity and international law. Do you see that last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I had simply wanted to pass on as a courtesy to the interpreters their request that references to the document be provided, but it seems that Mr. Karadzic is now doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Page 10, the last paragraph preceding the title "General Crimes." Do you agree that 46 criminal offences were registered pursuant to Chapter XVII of the Penal Code of Yugoslavia and those were crimes against humanity and international law which were committed in Teslic, Kupres, Knezevo and Kotor Varos and that 47 criminal reports were filed. And Sanski Most and Prijedor were excluded from this; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the document states, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I note the time. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1557, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll continue tomorrow. How much do you think you need to conclude your cross-examination, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I have a lot of documents. We will complete with the security centres and move on to the public security stations to see what they did. I hope to be able to finish within the next two sessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the time used by the Prosecution and the importance of the subject matter, the Chamber is minded to give you one more session tomorrow, that's it. And in the meantime, I'm going to come to the issue that we dealt with last Wednesday as to the admission of an intercept to which, i.e., 65 ter number 30115 to which Mr. Robinson objected to. While it is true that parties should, to the greatest extent possible, endeavour to use intercepts with witnesses who are participants in the intercepted conversations, this does not mean that -- that intercepts that were not so used cannot subsequently be marked for identification. I should also note that Mr. Robinson -- that the Defence itself has tendered a Mandic intercept following Mandic's testimony, which was then MFI'd by the Chamber. So accordingly, the Chamber will mark it for identification. We will give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI P2999, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So tomorrow we'll finish your evidence, Mr. Nielsen -- Dr. Nielsen. Tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 14th day of July, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.
